definitions.meaning: Concrete URL-specific evidence supports impersonation, credential theft or fraudulent inducement. Prefer phishing when both phishing and other malicious activity apply; retain other observations in signals.
Concrete evidence supports other malicious activity, such as malware delivery or exploitation; infrastructure anomalies alone are insufficient.
Actual observed risk signals exist but do not establish phishing or other malicious activity. High/critical requires concrete high-risk observations.
Sufficient evidence supports a legitimate purpose with no unresolved material threat signal within the investigation scope.
Essential evidence is missing, conflicting or unverifiable, preventing a reliable judgment.
